To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the combination of segmentation and detection networks is a powerful tool for word-level text spot-ting.

a) a fully convolutional network is able to detect text regions in the input image with high precision, and b) a second network that is able to predict word bounding boxes is able to accurately segment the image into individual words.
In summary, our research is concerned with

1) the design and implementation of an efficient, accurate and reliable text detection system, 2) the design and training of a word-level text spotting network, 3) the evaluation of our system against state-of-the-art systems on two standard benchmarks.
the following aspects:     - A novel algorithm for the accurate segmentation of text "in-the-wild".

the following questions: (i) how to design a network that is able to reliably and accurately detect regions of text in the wild; (ii) how to design an efficient architecture for the second stage of the pipeline that can reliably and accurately predict the bounding boxes of individual words.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed method is a very efficient, accurate and reliable text spotting algorithm, which is able to detect and recognize text "in the Wild".
our system is a good example of how to use a CNN to detect words in an image.

this paper proposes a new method to detect words in images, which has a high accuracy and is also able to detect words in the wild, which makes the proposed method very interesting and promising for future applications.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have achieved state-of-the-art performance on the two most popular word-level text spotting datasets, while maintaining real-time execution.

we are able to achieve a 0.5% improvement over state of the art in the ICDAR2013 dataset and an 11.7% improvement in the ICDR2015 dataset, which is a 2.5x improvement over the previous best performing method.
the proposed system achieves the state of the art results in word-level text spotting, while being fast and robust to the presence of non-text objects in the input images.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a simple cascade of two neural networks can outperform state-of-the-art methods, and that a fully convolutional network is sufficient for the first stage.
the segmentation of the text can be performed with a very high recall, even if the segmentation is not very accurate, and the subsequent word detection stage can be performed with high precision.
a simple and fast segmentation-detection network can outperform the more complex and slow end-to-end text spotter networks.
